meta.name: Exit-gate synthetic portfolio (one tenant, two sites, 24 h)
meta.description: Versioned exit-gate scenario for Phase 2 (P2.13/P2.25). All behaviour profiles are SYNTHETIC with stated assumptions - not validated physical models; all emitted telemetry is simulation-only (0.x line). A scenario change creates a NEW version; replay (P2.24) names this version + seed + code version. v2 (P2.25): adds the per-asset expected-quality plan (expected_quality) tied to the P2.15 fault types - the accounting input the exit-gate coverage check needs so injected MISSING intervals are distinguishable from unexplained gaps. v1 content is otherwise unchanged; the portfolio, horizon, cadence, seeds, and fault injections are byte-identical to v1. The faults section ships disabled (enabled=false), so the v2 exit-gate run remains all-GOOD with full per-asset coverage - fault logic is reachable only by enabling the plan in configuration.

behaviour_profile.assumptions: Synthetic rectangular-efficiency daily dispatch; no electrochemical, temperature, degradation, or state-of-health model; constant efficiency; no auxiliary consumption; instantaneous power transitions; availability constant true.

assets.capability_note: Reference only; curtailment is noted but NOT exercised in Phase 2 - no Phase 2 mechanism reduces PV output below the shape (P2.13 s5.2).

behaviour_profile.assumptions: Synthetic clear-sky cosine bell, zero at night; NO weather model (no clouds, irradiance series, or forecasts); no temperature, soiling, or derating model beyond the peak factor; no inverter clipping dynamics beyond the rated-power cap; fixed azimuth/tilt; availability constant true.

assets.capability_note: Reference only; the reducible range travels as scenario data for Phase 3 - no Phase 2 flexibility computation exists.

behaviour_profile.assumptions: Synthetic baseline shape (morning and evening peaks over a near-flat night); NO metered or measured data behind it; no weather or occupancy model; NO baseline method - the baseline is a scenario-declared shape, not a computed estimate (D1/D2 open); no per-appliance disaggregation; seeded jitter only.

Deterministic daily connection windows; NO mobility or traffic model (connections follow the declared windows, not arrival-time distributions); one aggregate EV per EVSE; constant charging efficiency; NO V2G discharge in Phase 2; instantaneous transitions at window boundaries; seeded jitter only.

Active power is the aggregated SUM of the site's assets' net active power at each tick - a consistency fixture; a real PCC meter would include non-modelled load and losses. Reactive power is a configured constant under the site's declared convention.

horizon.clock_note: The scenario clock is deterministic simulation time (P0.09 s5), distinct from wall-clock time. Window and curve times are scenario-clock UTC.

cadence.default_note: 1-minute default (D-SC3): 1440 samples/asset/day - enough for freshness, staleness, bucketing, and partitioning coverage at a volume the pipeline handles without backpressure drama. Per-asset overrides possible; none used in v1.

seeds.derivation_note: One master seed plus a recorded per-asset derivation rule (D-SC4): adding an asset in a future version does not perturb existing assets' streams. The RNG algorithm and seed handling are recorded with the simulator (P2.14 step 2). Profiles without randomness (PV clear-sky, baseline shapes) consume no randomness.

faults.note: P2.15 fault-injection plan: per-asset, per-interval scenario configuration - never ad-hoc code paths. SOURCE-level outcomes: drop = no frame for the interval (absence; the platform's gap detector synthesizes MISSING, P2.04 D-T6); delay = frame released delay_seconds late on the scenario clock, so its age (release - event_time) exceeds freshness_limit_seconds and the P2.08 staleness rule marks it STALE downstream; out_of_range = active power scaled by factor past the rated limit, source code OUT_OF_RANGE -> SUSPECT; source_invalid = source code SOURCE_INVALID -> BAD; duplicate = identical re-emission under the same identity; out_of_order = frame held hold_ticks and released after a later tick's frame; conflicting_duplicate = re-emission under the same identity with a different value. All arithmetic is scenario-clock arithmetic. SCOPE: these are simulator faults for testing the platform's handling - they are NOT claims about real device failure modes.

expected_quality.plan_note: P2.25 per-asset expected-quality plan: the expected STORED outcome per injected asset over the 24-hour horizon, tied one-to-one to the P2.15 fault types in faults.injections. With faults disabled (the exit-gate default) every asset expects GOOD at every tick and full coverage (1440 ticks per emitted quantity per asset). With the fault plan enabled, each entry below names the expected DEVIATION inside its window; every tick outside every window stays GOOD. expected_quality_in_window is the quality state the platform is expected to end up with for that window: drop produces NO frame, so the interval is covered only by the gap detector's synthesized MISSING markers (P2.04 D-T6) and the coverage accounting credits it as an EXPECTED gap - never as an unexplained one. All other fault types still emit one value per tick, so they do not reduce coverage; their expected states are recorded so stored states can be checked against the plan rather than guessed.

per_asset.expected_note: the exact duplicate is acknowledged (P2.09); exactly one stored row per tick
the held frame is stored late; arrival order never changes the stored quality (P2.09)
the conflicting copy is quarantined with a reason (P2.09); the original row stands
